title: Fixed-Q Frobenius-class rho: S0 constant parking, work cap 125.1169

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in proof.md (compute g=e(P0,Q); solve z=g^x by distinguished-point Pollard rho with 2^20 walks advanced round-robin on one processor on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT with R=1024 twisted multipliers, a 4-multiplication canonical-conjugate key, a Granger-Scott cyclotomic-squaring branch with nominal heuristic probability 37/64 (a step squares iff the 6-bit branch field T mod 64 is below 37; branch, multiplier and distinguished-point bits read from the free class invariant T=Re(c_0), so the squaring update needs no keys; the 12 keys are computed on multiply steps and at distinguished points only; the 12-key minimum is full-width, charged 200 worst-case), deterministic fruitless-cycle escapes, hard caps on reports, restarts and matcher pairs, and a pre-debit work meter whose walk-phase budget leaves a reserved stopping allowance (so the work bound holds on every run); output P=[x]P0 and verify e(P,Q)=z) succeeds, in the ideal model, with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^125.1169 total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents (C=20,000), including setup, pairings, table construction, walk starts, distinguished-point handling, cycle handling, detection delay, matching (the sort, duplicate removal and pair checks), output and verification. The table multiply is a fixed-multiplier kernel of 14,398 executed instructions (0.7199 units; each Fp6 coordinate of the two half products summed once), below the 20,000-instruction reference operation; the 54 Karatsuba pre-sums it stores per table entry (2,592 bytes) are built in the charged table construction, inside its 2^20.2-unit item; the branch, distinguished-point and key-minimum rule is stated on the limbs as stored by the pinned blst kernels (Montgomery form x*2^384 mod p), so the priced operations read exactly the representation the rule names and no conversion is charged; the squaring branch is priced at the executed count of the straight-line kernel kernels/sqr.s, 6,752 scalar instructions per call (pool p parked once in six idle S0 registers; the six single-limb const-keys chain it from registers) (branch-free scalar AArch64; kernels/gen.py, emu.py and check_kernels.py regenerate and check it; measured blst baseline 9,803 in measure/), plus 226 instructions of bookkeeping carried by every step (213 itemised, plus 8 for the 192-bit work meter, which runs its full 3-word pre-debit compare before every step and then adds the step charge, and 5 for the 2-word stuck-walk counter: adds/adc, then a mov of 5120 into a register, a cmp of its high word with it and a branch, exact since 20/theta = 5120 * 2^64), so a squaring step is 6,978 instructions (0.3489 unit); multiply steps are 14,398 kernel + 226 + 2,014 key = 16,638 instructions (0.8319 unit); the walk costs 0.552665625 units per step, the ledger total is below 2^125.09186 and the submitted bound 2^125.1169 is the least 1/20,000-bit grid point that also covers a 2-percentage-point drop of the squaring fraction at these prices. Before every charged action of the walk phase (a step, an escape, a report, a switch, a walk start or restart) the meter is compared with a threshold that leaves room for that action's largest charge; the action runs only if the meter is below the threshold (a carry-only 192-bit compare, cmp/sbcs/sbcs/b.hs, branching exactly when the meter is at or above it), and the meter then adds its charge. The walk-phase budget is 2^125.1169 units minus the 2^31-unit setup bound and a reserved stopping allowance below 2^53.55 units that covers matching at its worst case, output, verification and halting, so setup, walk phase and stopping phase together do at most 2^125.1169 units on every run, an inequality experiment.py checks on integers. The meter's bookkeeping at walk starts (below 2^11.04 units) and restarts (below 2^27.04 units) and the 600-instruction switches between 2^63-step chunks (below 2^58.59 units) are charged; restarts are capped once at 2^36 against an expected count below 2^27.29, counted per gap between consecutive reports (the stuck-walk counter resets at every report, a 4-instruction charge inside the 4,000-instruction report item, and at every start and restart), and the meter pays for the whole cap; a run past the cap is a cap failure inside the 0.01 allowance. The distinguished-point rate is theta = 2^-72 (a class is distinguished iff bits 16 to 87 of T are zero; the fingerprint is bits 88 to 215), and the report cap 2^55 bounds reports, so every address, index and report count fits one native 64-bit word; the stuck-walk threshold 20/theta = 20*2^72 and the work meter are the only multiword counters, with their carry chains priced. Reports are appended to a log of exactly 2^55 slots of 80 bytes with no pointer field (2^61.322 bytes; no sharding and no multiword address), addressed by the one-word report counter; reaching the cap fails the run, a cap failure inside the 0.01 allowance. Matching runs once, after the walk phase: an in-place heapsort of the whole record (at most 54 x 2^55 + 57 levels at 132 instructions, below 2^53.53 units), one adjacent comparison per record for exact duplicates, and every pair inside each run of equal fingerprints under a hard budget of 2^16 pairs whose overflow fails the run (the expected number of false-key pairs is at most 2^-19 by linearity of expectation, so Markov gives 2^-35), halting at the first verifying pair. The sort, dedup and scan read only slots a report wrote, so the log needs no initialisation (the operating system's zero-fill of fresh 2 MiB pages on first write is charged inside the 4,000-instruction report item, 13 instructions per record), and no report is dropped before the cap. Peak memory is below 2^63 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^31 units (the setup items) and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. Every fresh scalar modulo r (the table's two per multiplier, and (alpha,beta) at each walk start and restart) is drawn by one bounded sampler in the ideal model (the ChaCha20 keystream, in the 64-bit-counter/64-bit-nonce layout, is assumed indistinguishable from an ideal random source; no bound on the sampled scalars is claimed). An attempt takes 255 bits from one 64-byte block, charged 2,300 instructions (itemised: 80 quarter-rounds, feed-forward, 16-word loads/stores, counter adds/adc, address set-up, spill margin; 1,270 in all), and accepts the four-word draw X iff X < r by a carry-only compare (20 instructions); an attempt's fixed maximum is 2,320 instructions and a sample's is R_MAX=256 attempts, 593,920 instructions = 29.696 units. X is 255 bits and 2^254<r<2^255, so acceptance is above 1/2; after 256 rejects the sampler returns the fixed residue 1 (the exhaustion rule), with probability at most 2^-256 per sample and 2^-218.99 over a run's below 2^37.01 samples under the ideal-source model, carried as an exhaustion allowance of 2^-218.99 in the success budget. The seed and state are initialised in setup inside the 2^31-unit bound; the table item charges its 2,048 draws and each start and restart its two (59.392 units), so every sampling action has a fixed maximum. The success bound relies on the standard random-mapping heuristic for rho walks, adjusted for the branch mix (effective class count N/(1-s^2-(1-s)^2/R)), with model success 0.4005 (at least 0.3904 after the 0.01 for H1+ and the small terms) against the required 0.39, supported by toy-field experiments and by running the production branch rule with a 16-entry table and no distinguished-point test in the real GT; the threshold ending the walk phase early and the firing of the caps are covered by the heuristic H1+ (no percentage-point drift of the branch, cycle and report statistics over the run) with a budget of 0.01 of success probability; no production-size run is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Part A: BLS12-381 GT identities (Re(c_0) across the 12 conjugates, Frobenius formula, 4-multiplication key, distinctness, canonical representative, Granger-Scott squaring counts, r-1 factorisation). Part C: the production branch rule (T mod 64, low table-index bits) on real GT for 2,000 steps per rule vs explicit Frobenius. Part B: the complete algorithm (cycle escapes, report log, heapsort matcher, pair budget, collision solving) in a toy field vs the branch-adjusted random-mapping law. Part E: pair-collision law. Part D: read measure/, assert the blst marginals and kernel prices, recompute the ledger, caps, cap inequality, matcher worst case, stopping allowance and non-walk sum. Part S: the bounded sampler. flags_check.py: the multiword compares/increments under AArch64 NZCV. Toy scale only; no production costs.
